candidates.title: Narrow-alley infill sites steering tenant mix away from retail
candidates.shift: A commercial building on a sub-6-metre alley site is explicitly designed to favor quiet offices and tenants who value parking over street-frontage retail visibility.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: single-instance signal that narrow urban infill parcels may get steered toward office/quiet-tenant use rather than retail, gradually reshaping ground-floor commercial mix in dense cities.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily profile of HOURS Commercial Building (See Architects) notes the alley site 'favors...tenants who value parking over' street frontage.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of site-constraint-driven tenant sorting, where narrow infill lots push commercial use away from retail toward office/parking-oriented tenants. If common, it would quietly shrink retail's footprint in dense infill fabric.
candidates.author: Pratik Mour

candidates.title: Warehouse vernacular reused for civic/community infrastructure
candidates.shift: A new waterfront community centre borrows form and materials from traditional maritime warehouse/coastal-shelter typologies.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: single instance suggesting rising demand for community-connection space on port-adjacent redevelopment sites, referencing industrial vernacular rather than generic civic architecture.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen feature on AOR Architects' Talas community centre in Helsinki, informed by maritime warehouses and coastal shelters.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of place-based vernacular reuse for placemaking on former industrial/port land; if it spreads, waterfront brownfield redevelopment could increasingly favor civic/community programming over pure commercial.
candidates.author: Jon Astbury

candidates.title: Leftover mall/food-court corners reactivated as destination spaces
candidates.shift: A residual, unused corner of a food court is redesigned into a standalone restaurant with its own identity rather than left as dead space.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: single instance pointing to a strategy for underperforming mall real estate — reactivating 'leftover' retail space as a differentiated anchor instead of demolition or vacancy.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily profile of Restaurant Nectar Oum (Madarq studio), converting a 'leftover corner of a food court' using a borrowed garden concept.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of value-extraction from dead retail space through identity-driven food/community programming, relevant to mall owners facing vacancy pressure from eComm competition.
candidates.author: Cristina Popescu

candidates.title: Handcrafted regional materials resurging in flagship retail design
candidates.shift: A Tokyo design studio clads a Seoul department-store flagship in handcrafted Korean celadon tiles, foregrounding artisanal regional material over generic global retail finishes.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: single instance, but could signal a shift toward local/artisanal material sourcing in flagship store construction for brand differentiation, with implications for trade-skill demand.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen feature on I IN's Human Made store in Lotte Mall Jamsil, Seoul, clad in handcrafted Korean celadon tiles.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of retail fit-out sourcing shifting from generic global materials toward regional craft, driven by brand differentiation. If it spreads, store construction could re-localize demand for artisan trades.
candidates.author: Cajsa Carlson

candidates.title: 'Semi-open park commercial complex' emerges as hybrid retail typology
candidates.shift: A new named commercial format blending street-retail frontage with open park/naturalistic landscape debuts in Guangzhou, China.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could signal an emerging mixed-use retail typology — park-integrated, semi-open commercial development as an alternative to enclosed malls — with China setting rather than following the format.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily coverage of Aranya's 'first semi-open park commercial complex,' Aranya Guangzhou Jiulong Lake, described as raw concrete street-side retail.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of retail real estate moving from enclosed-mall logic to open, park-integrated commercial formats; if it takes hold, it could reshape how developers plan mixed-use retail land in dense Asian cities and beyond.
candidates.author: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang

candidates.title: Remediated industrial land reborn as public climate-amenity landmark
candidates.shift: A former industrial/mining site in Sweden is redeveloped into a public 'climate action park,' with a symbolic crystal-shaped sauna as its first permanent structure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: single instance modeling brownfield-to-civic-amenity conversion; could foreshadow how developers repurpose contaminated or defunct industrial/retail-adjacent land as branded public space.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen coverage of Lithium Crystal Sauna, first permanent structure at WasteLand Climate Action Park on a remediated industrial site in Skellefteå, Sweden.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of remediated industrial land shifting from liability to civic/branded amenity asset, driven by climate-park placemaking. If scaled, brownfield real estate could become a source of public/retail-adjacent value rather than pure environmental cost.
candidates.author: Rheanna Hopkins

candidates.title: Computer-vision crowd behavior analysis extends beyond loss prevention
candidates.shift: A CV system (Modified YOLOv4-tiny) for crowd detection and behavior analysis is proposed for public safety in crowded business areas.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: already widely covered as loss-prevention/surveillance tech, but framing here extends toward behavior analysis for staffing/safety decisions in crowded retail environments — included for calibration, likely Context.
candidates.evidence: Paper introduces a Modified YOLOv4-tiny-based Intelligent Crowd Analysis system for detection and behavior analysis in surveillance video.
candidates.source: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of computer vision maturing from simple counting to behavior inference in physical spaces; if adopted in stores, could shift staffing and safety operations toward real-time crowd-behavior triggers.
candidates.author: GANTA RAJU, Gs Naveen Kumar

candidates.title: BIM/IFC workflows becoming default sustainability documentation layer
candidates.shift: Building Information Modeling with IFC-based data standards is increasingly required for eco-efficient, low-carbon construction compliance globally.
candidates.ai_read: Trend — already a well-established push in construction digitization; included so Kristen can distinguish genuine shift from now-baseline practice.
candidates.evidence: Study on bridging BIM and sustainability, examining global trends and information requirements for IFC-based workflows.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of construction documentation shifting from siloed drawings to interoperable, carbon-tracked digital models; if it becomes universal, permitting and financing could start requiring BIM-based carbon disclosure.
candidates.author: Lucas Andrade Nunes, José Maria Franco de CARVALHO, Guilherme Palla Teixeira et al.

candidates.title: Indoor environmental quality hardening from amenity to baseline requirement
candidates.shift: A systematic review signals growing consensus that IEQ improvements (air, light, thermal comfort) are becoming a required standard for occupant health, not an optional amenity.
candidates.ai_read: Trend-adjacent: IEQ focus already established in wellness-building discourse; flagged because it may soon translate into harder certification requirements affecting store/workplace design.
candidates.evidence: Frontiers in Built Environment systematic review of IEQ intervention strategies for enhancing occupant comfort.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of building comfort standards moving from voluntary wellness branding toward baseline occupant-health requirement; could eventually reshape HVAC/lighting specs and labor retention arguments for retail employers.
candidates.author: Emmanuel Chongcicimmi Ibrahim, Amusan Lekan, Andrew Mhya Stanley

candidates.title: Occupant-behavior-aware simulation could reset building energy compliance models
candidates.shift: A new model incorporates subjective occupant factors (cost consideration, accessibility) into device-usage simulation for more realistic building performance prediction.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: incremental academic refinement, but if adopted could change how developers model and certify building energy performance, altering design and compliance decisions.
candidates.evidence: Paper proposes a Multi-Device Occupant Behavior model combined with an OODA-loop approach for improved building performance prediction.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of building-performance modeling shifting from idealized to behaviorally realistic assumptions; if standardized, could change energy-code compliance testing for new retail/commercial buildings.
candidates.author: Gaoxiang Chen, Long Chen, Qiuchen Lu et al.

candidates.title: Reinforcement learning maturing for joint solar+battery site management
candidates.shift: RL is increasingly applied to jointly optimize photovoltaic generation and battery dispatch, moving beyond simple maximum-power-point tracking.
candidates.ai_read: Trend: RL for PV/battery optimization is an active, well-covered research area; flagged because it converges with store-level on-site energy/compute autonomy questions in the 'compute?' hunt zone.
candidates.evidence: Systematic literature review on reinforcement learning for integrated MPPT and battery management in PV systems.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of energy management shifting from static rule-based control to autonomous AI dispatch; if deployed at store/warehouse scale, it could reduce grid dependency and reshape utility contracts.
candidates.author: Francisco Fidalgo, Ramiro S. Barbosa

candidates.title: Software-enabled Renewable Energy Communities as alternative site power procurement
candidates.shift: A review of software and algorithms underpinning Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) shows growing infrastructure for localized, collectively-owned energy production/consumption.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could let retail sites join collectively-owned local energy production or microgrids, altering utility contracting and infrastructure investment — relevant to the 'compute?'/utilities hunt zone.
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of software programs and algorithms for implementing Renewable Energy Communities.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of energy procurement decentralizing from utility-only contracts toward community-owned generation; if it scales, store real estate could become a node in shared local energy markets rather than a passive grid consumer.
candidates.author: Matilde Chierici, Martina Ferrando, Sibilla Ferroni et al.

candidates.title: Maritime circularity lag could bottleneck freight decarbonization
candidates.shift: A review finds circular-economy adoption across shipbuilding and vessel lifecycles remains fragmented despite pressure to decarbonize.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: slow maritime circularity could keep ocean freight costs/emissions elevated, indirectly pressuring retail supply-chain delivery-format decisions — touches the 'delivery format?' hunt zone.
candidates.evidence: Frontiers in Marine Science systematic review of barriers, digital enablers, and transition frameworks for circular economy in maritime industrial processes.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of upstream freight infrastructure lagging behind sustainability pressure; if maritime circularity stalls, retailers relying on ocean freight may face rising cost/emissions exposure, pushing reconsideration of delivery formats and near-shoring.
candidates.author: Rasa Ziliene, Henrika Ruginė, Jaroslav Dvorak

candidates.title: AI-driven land allocation could reshape zoning logic in China's rural-urban integration
candidates.shift: AI is being applied to optimize national land-resource allocation for food/ecological security and rural-urban integration.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could presage AI-assisted zoning/land-use decision systems affecting where commercial/retail development is permitted, particularly under China's urban-rural integration push.
candidates.evidence: Study 'From Mismatch to Smart Match: Artificial Intelligence and Land Resource Misallocation' published in Land.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of land-use governance shifting from administrative/manual zoning toward algorithmic allocation; if it spreads, it could reset how quickly and on what criteria land gets rezoned for commercial/retail use.
candidates.author: Long Xin, Yidan Liu, Yuyao Wang et al.

candidates.title: Blockchain real estate vehicles emerging where traditional REITs failed
candidates.shift: Indonesia is exploring a blockchain-based real estate investment ecosystem after its REIT-equivalent (DIRE) failed to develop into a liquid market.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a peripheral market experimenting with tokenized real-estate capital-raising as an end-run around failed conventional REIT structures — worth watching as a potential alternative financing template.
candidates.evidence: Humanities and Social Sciences Communications study designing a blockchain real estate investment ecosystem for Indonesia, noting DIRE's underdevelopment versus REITs elsewhere.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of emerging markets bypassing failed conventional real-estate finance structures via blockchain tokenization; if it works, it could offer a new capital-raising template for retail real estate in markets lacking liquid REIT markets.
candidates.author: Gunawan Wang, Surjo Sastroharjono, Deshinta Arrova Dewi et al.

candidates.title: Ceramic construction/demolition waste reprocessed into new tile feedstock
candidates.shift: Waste ceramic sanitaryware and broken tiles from construction/demolition are being characterized as viable 'grog' feedstock for new sustainable ceramic tile production in Nigeria.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could seed new circular-material supply chains for building finishes, reducing virgin material demand, with a developing-country geography leading the reuse practice rather than following one.
candidates.evidence: Geochemical/mineralogical characterization of ceramic sanitary waste as grog for sustainable ceramic tile production using XRF/XRD analyses, Nigeria.
candidates.source: Journal of Biodiversity and Environmental Research
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of construction-waste circularity moving from aspiration to material science, converting demolition ceramic waste into new building-finish inputs; if scaled, it could lower cost and carbon of tile sourcing for store fit-outs.
candidates.author: EMMANUEL OLADIMEJI, Abdullahi A. Umar, ENOCH G. WURITKA et al.

candidates.title: Compounding heat vulnerabilities force differentiated urban design responses
candidates.shift: Research identifies overlapping/compounding vulnerabilities to heat among marginalized populations, requiring adaptation strategies beyond average heat-mitigation design.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could push building/urban design toward targeted heat-resilience interventions (cooling infrastructure, retrofit priority) for multiply-vulnerable populations — an equity-driven physical-space requirement.
candidates.evidence: Study on adaptation strategies of people experiencing multiple vulnerabilities to heat in Vienna, Österreichische Zeitschrift für Soziologie.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of climate-adaptation design shifting from uniform heat-mitigation to vulnerability-differentiated interventions; if adopted by planners, it could reshape where cooling infrastructure, shade, and retrofit investment gets prioritized around stores and public space.
candidates.author: Raphaela Kogler, Nadine Haufe, Fidelia Gartner et al.

candidates.title: Rising humidity intensifies deadly heat risk in Africa's Great Green Wall region
candidates.shift: New research finds increased atmospheric moisture is amplifying hazardous humid-heat conditions along the Sahel's Great Green Wall belt, beyond dry-heat assumptions.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: construction/outdoor labor scheduling and building cooling needs in the Sahel may need urgent rethinking as wet-bulb thresholds approach dangerous levels — a peripheral-geography early warning for global heat-safety standards.
candidates.evidence: Research Square preprint 'Increased Moisture Amplifies Hazardous Humid-Heat in Africa's Great Green Wall.'
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of climate hazard reclassification — from dry heat to compound humid-heat risk — in a region undergoing major land-restoration/construction investment; if confirmed, outdoor labor codes and building cooling requirements across the Sahel could need rapid revision.
candidates.author: Cascade Tuholske, Catherine Ivanovich, Emily Williams et al.
